evidence_quotes.quote: En el Municipio de Puerto Vallarta, el ejercicio de los derechos de acceso al agua potable y saneamiento, se promueve a través de un servicio público municipal, cuya contratación implica el pago de los costos de conexión, las cuotas correspondientes y la suscripción del contrato de prestación de servicios con base al artículo 9 del RPSPAPDATDARMPV y lo establecido en la Ley de Ingresos del Municipio.

El artículo 46 del RPSPAPDATDARMPV establece una lista de las cuotas y tarifa que deben pagar los usuarios para el acceso a los servicios públicos, con base a los montos regulados en la Ley de Ingresos del Municipio de Puerto Vallarta del 2025, los cuales se aplican al régimen del servicio medido en usuarios domésticos, comercial, industrial y hoteleros, con cuotas mínimas, costos crecientes y costos totales con base a los metros cúbicos (m3) de agua potable que consuman los usuarios de acuerdo al artículo 52 del RPSPAPDATDARMPV (tabla 2).

La asequibilidad de las tarifas se promueve a su vez con las disposiciones del capítulo VII del RPSPAPDATDARMPV, que establecen subsidios para instituciones de asistencia social y uso doméstico, sin que estos rebasen el 50% de los costos del consumo y previo el cumplimiento de requisitos correspondientes, como se señala en la tabla 4.

El primer muestreo a usuarios domésticos, doméstico residencial, Comerciales e Industriales (D.C.I.) y el segundo, a usuarios hoteleros con una muestra de 364 usuarios D.C.I. y 100 usuarios hoteleros.
Aun cuando el 60% de los usuarios D.C.I. manifiestan que el costo es accesible, se tiene al 38% que afirman costos elevados con 137 usuarios en este último porcentaje

el 66.20% de los usuarios D.C.I. se sienten seguros de contar con agua al hacer el pago por el suministro y 33.80% de estos usuarios afirman que dicho pago no les asegura el poder disponer del recurso hídrico.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines household/domestic (as well as domestic-residential, commercial, industrial, and hotel) access to municipal drinking water and wastewater sanitation services provided by SEAPAL-VALLARTA in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Plain reading: analyzes national, state, and municipal water legislation and utility regulation (Ley de Aguas Nacionales, Ley Federal de Derechos 2024, LAEJM, Ley de Ingresos del Municipio de Puerto Vallarta 2025, and municipal utility regulation RPSPAPDATDARMPV). Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: directly examines tariff and cost-recovery rules governing service access, including connection fees and service contracting requirements (Arts. 9, 44, 57, 58 RPSPAPDATDARMPV; Art. 56 Ley de Ingresos, Table 1), metered increasing-block tariff structures (cuota mínima, costo creciente, costo total under Arts. 46 and 52 RPSPAPDATDARMPV, Table 2), and domestic tariff subsidy caps and eligibility/tenure/documentation rules (Chapter VII RPSPAPDATDARMPV, Table 4, requiring Mexican citizenship, owner or tenant status, residence, income qualification, no payment arrears, and consumption <= 60 m3 bimonthly).
criterion_notes.c3: Cross-sectional socio-legal empirical study combining doctrinal/regulatory analysis with primary survey data from two stratified random samples of SEAPAL-VALLARTA utility users (n = 364 domestic, domestic-residential, commercial, and industrial [D.C.I.] users sampled via QGIS across neighborhoods and n = 100 hotel users from the utility's user list, out of N = 88,686 total users), analyzed using descriptive statistics and contingency tables in SPSS 2021.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports empirical outcomes directly relevant to affordability, quantity, and reliability/security of access: self-reported tariff payment brackets and corresponding water consumption regimes (89.83% of D.C.I. users in the increasing-cost tariff tier), perceived tariff affordability (60% of D.C.I. users report accessible costs vs. 38% reporting elevated costs), and perceived security of water supply availability upon paying tariffs (66.20% of D.C.I. users feel secure of having water upon paying vs. 33.80% stating payment does not guarantee supply, compared with 91% vs. 9% among hotel users).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and unit of analysis (utility user accounts/households and establishments of SEAPAL-VALLARTA in Puerto Vallarta, N = 88,686; stratified random samples n = 364 D.C.I. users and n = 100 hotel users, with visual disaggregation of domestic and domestic-residential users in figures), legal/tariff exposure, access/affordability outcomes, and cross-sectional survey + regulatory study design are all clearly identifiable. Note for synthesis: quantitative text percentages pool D.C.I. (domestic, domestic-residential, commercial, industrial) users together while bar charts disaggregate domestic subgroups, so this study definitely qualifies for systematic review inclusion even if subgroup-specific numbers require care for quantitative meta-analysis.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with English title and abstract on pp. 1-2). Per Inclusion Criterion 10, other languages may be included when translation is feasible and the study is potentially important: full-text translation from Spanish is directly feasible from the provided 24-page PDF, and the study provides primary socio-legal empirical evidence on municipal water/sanitation tariff rules, connection fees, subsidy eligibility criteria, and affordability/supply security; log translation method and translator in `extraction_note` during data extraction.

study_design: Cross-sectional socio-legal regulatory analysis and stratified random user survey
population_and_sample: Registered utility users (accounts/households and commercial/industrial/hotel establishments) of SEAPAL-VALLARTA in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico (finite population N = 88,686 users; two stratified random samples of n = 364 domestic, domestic-residential, commercial, and industrial [D.C.I.] users and n = 100 hotel users)
exposure: Statutory economic valuation of water and municipal tariff, connection-fee, increasing-block pricing, and domestic subsidy eligibility rules (Ley de Aguas Nacionales, Ley Federal de Derechos 2024, Ley de Ingresos del Municipio de Puerto Vallarta 2025, and RPSPAPDATDARMPV)
outcome: Approximate water and sanitation tariff expenditures and consumption tiers, user-perceived tariff affordability (accessible vs. elevated cost), and perceived security/continuity of water supply upon tariff payment
rationale: This 2026 empirical socio-legal study in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico satisfies all systematic-review inclusion criteria under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. It analyzes concrete legal and regulatory rules governing municipal drinking water and sanitation access—specifically connection fees, service contracting requirements, increasing-block volumetric tariffs, and domestic subsidy caps and eligibility/tenure requirements under the municipal utility regulation (RPSPAPDATDARMPV) and 2025 Municipal Revenue Law—alongside primary stratified random survey data (n = 364 D.C.I. users and n = 100 hotel users) measuring tariff payment tiers, perceived tariff affordability, and perceived supply security upon payment. Although written in Spanish (with an English abstract), full-text translation is directly feasible per Criterion 10.
